solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Another bloody hold-up!

parts.note: reads like a weary complaint about yet another traffic jam or robbery, but means a device that holds up the flow of blood

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' is a British mild swear word in the surface, but literally means involving blood; the 'hold-up' is stopping its flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight band that stops bleeding from a wound literally holds up the blood.

clue.text: Curved shape in which square cuts are made

definitions.text: in which square cuts are made
definitions.meaning: A London cricket ground, and a square cut is a cricket stroke

explanation.definitionFit: An egg-shaped outline is also the name of a famous London cricket ground.

clue.text: New aide or anyone responsible for kit on group tour

definitions.text: anyone responsible for kit on group tour

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A new assistant or someone else looks after a band's equipment on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges AIDE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A road crew member sets up and carries the equipment for a touring band.

clue.text: This turns out to sum up Panama, for example

indicators.note: turns out signals the letters are turned into a different order

explanation.surface: This proves to summarise Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges THIS and SUM together; 'to' and 'up' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a narrow strip of land joining two larger masses, an example of the term.

clue.text: Could such a description be fair comment?

definitions.text: Could such a description be fair comment?

parts.words: Could such a description be fair comment?
parts.note: fair comment is a legal phrase, but fair also means beautiful, and a description that is the opposite of beautiful would not be

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the opposite of fair in the sense of good-looking.

clue.text: As an example King Lear grew old in the attempt

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: an attempt is a try
aged means grew old

explanation.surface: King Lear aged while trying, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear grows old in Shakespeare's play, so the surface sits naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Lear is a classic instance of the dramatic genre ending in catastrophe.

clue.text: Mixes drink for a fund-raiser

parts.note: jumbles means mixes up
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone blends drinks for a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A British sale of donated second-hand goods raises money for a cause.

clue.text: A colt needs breaking as a youngster

indicators.note: breaking signals the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A young horse must be broken in while still young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks like training a horse, but rearranges COLT NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Money for some tobacco

definitions.meaning: British slang for a pound sterling
a lump of chewing tobacco held in the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both British slang for a pound coin and a plug of tobacco for chewing.

clue.text: Dance with sailor before everyone retires

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word for everyone is read backwards

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A dance with a sailor before the whole company goes to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' suggests going to bed, but here it turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast whirling Italian folk dance in six-eight time.

clue.text: Frisk doctor entering prison

indicators.note: the doctor goes into the prison, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is searched as he walks into a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' looks like the police search, but it means to leap about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk is to skip and leap playfully, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: In poor condition, we're heard to ask for sympathy

indicators.note: what is said aloud is the plea, and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: the plea a group might make for compassion: pity us

explanation.surface: People in a bad way are overheard begging for compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're' sets up the plea as spoken by us: 'pity us', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitiful or wretched is in a sorry, deplorable state that deserves pity.

clue.text: Supervise a review that is influential

indicators.note: review suggests a re-view, a second look in which the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Supervising an appraisal is a powerful thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' rearranges SUPERVISE A; 'that is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something persuasive is convincing and able to influence people.

clue.text: Agrees to a wage cut and drowns one's sorrows

definitions.meaning: has a drink, as in a drop of whisky

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to accept less pay and to have a little alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Reports it's very warm on board

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so one piece goes within

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is aboard
very warm means hot

explanation.surface: Someone reports how warm it is aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention for inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports here are bangs from guns, the sounds of shots being fired.

clue.text: Speech might indicate where one's home is

definitions.meaning: a formal talk given to an audience

definitions.text: might indicate where one's home is
definitions.meaning: the street, town and postcode written on letters

explanation.surface: A talk could reveal where the speaker lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal talk and the location details of a residence.

clue.text: Medal for conflict in our time

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A medal given for fighting in a modern war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our time' is the current era, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is a prize or honour given in recognition.

clue.text: Why so unusually ostentatious?

indicators.note: in an unusual arrangement, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a person is being so strangely flashy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' reorders the letters of WHY SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and ostentatious both describe a flashy display meant to attract notice.

clue.text: Lean Lothario?

definitions.meaning: to slope or incline, as a stage or mast does
a seducer of women, after a character in an 18th-century play

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a slope or incline and a dissolute womaniser.

clue.text: Made out to be a lady

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is portrayed as a refined woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman given a British honour, or simply an old-fashioned word for a lady.

clue.text: They guide Southern sailors

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south or southern
tars is an old word for sailors

explanation.surface: Navigators in the southern seas are steered by something.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors navigated by these celestial bodies, so the definition sits in the same scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of light in the night sky long guided navigators at sea.

clue.text: Puts off one's retirement

parts.note: reads as delaying leaving work, but means delaying going to bed

explanation.definitionFit: Not going to bed until late means remaining awake and out of it.

clue.text: One sort of shirt used as a vest

parts.note: single means one
a T is a kind of shirt, the T-shirt

explanation.surface: A kind of shirt worn as an undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: A vest in Britain is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless athletic top is also called a vest in British English.

clue.text: Outvotes?

parts.note: reads as beats in a ballot, but means votes someone out of their position, as in an election defeat

explanation.definitionFit: Voting a member out of parliament removes them from their place in the house.

clue.text: Refuse to agree to a climb-down, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for the climb-down is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: a climb-down is a descent from a height

explanation.surface: Someone will not accept a humiliating backing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb-down' looks like a retreat in an argument, but is taken literally as a descent.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to disagree or refuse to accept a view.

clue.text: Sort of boxer dog?

definitions.meaning: one who spars against an imaginary opponent

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a boxer practising alone and means to follow someone secretly.

clue.text: A man called for Australian port

indicators.note: called signals that the name is said aloud

parts.note: Sidney is a man's first name

explanation.surface: A man is summoned to an Australian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' looks like naming, but means said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in New South Wales, with its famous harbour.

clue.text: Tie up fifty-one

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A tie of fifty-one, as in a sporting score.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace shoes is to tie them up with cords.

clue.text: Charge for ring

definitions.meaning: a fee for using a road or bridge

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fee for passage and the slow sounding of a bell.

clue.text: Bolted after the horse — it's too late!

definitions.text: Bolted after the horse — it's too late!

parts.words: Bolted after the horse — it's too late!
parts.note: plays on the proverb about locking up only after the animal has run away

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says it is useless to shut the barn's entrance once the animal has fled.

clue.text: Six look back on a big fiddle

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: back means the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Six people glance back at a large-scale swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a fraud, but here means a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A Renaissance bowed stringed instrument, the larger kinds resembling a cello.

clue.text: Close to being an attractive watering place

parts.note: attractive means pretty
a well is where water is drawn

explanation.surface: Something is nearly a charming spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watering place' suggests a spa town, but is just a well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means almost or very nearly, as in 'nearly finished'.
